core.title: Scope each planner run to one slice with per-invocation framing
core.given: A planner invocation targets a scoped slice (the plan-artifact root may be empty or may hold artifacts from earlier runs).
core.when: You frame and decompose the plan for this invocation.
core.then: Plan only this invocation's scoped slice, with framing derived for this invocation.
prefer: Treat framing as per-invocation: different runs have different framing.
When the plan-artifact root already holds artifacts, read them via the repo graph to compose with them.
avoid: Any atdd agent ask (not in this protocol).
Any step-1 disk persistence (not in this protocol).
Creating or using the plan metadata file designated by the profile, and no other metadata file (not in this protocol).
Any coach involvement (not in this protocol).
Widening the run beyond its scoped slice.
core.why: Each invocation targets a scoped slice and different runs have different framing, so framing must come from this run and the graph rather than be carried over from earlier runs.
evidence: The run's plan output covers only the invoked slice.
When the plan-artifact root existed, the transcript shows it was read via the repo graph before composing.
No framing carried over from a prior run.
No atdd agent ask, no step-1 disk persistence, no plan metadata file designated by the profile, and no coach involvement anywhere in the run.
verification: The check enforces the obligation generically: one scoped slice per planner run, with framing per-invocation, read from the repository graph, not inherited.

The exclusions in avoid are unqualified: they apply anywhere in the run, not only to framing. The metadata-file exclusion is bounded to the single file designated by the profile; it forbids no other metadata file.

The excluded mechanism that is diff-observable (creating the designated plan metadata file, by its profile-given path) is a mechanical finding; the other excluded mechanisms and inherited framing are judged from the transcript.

Activation is known at dispatch from the role/operation: every planner decomposition invocation fires the rule, including first runs with no existing plan artifacts and runs whose task text has no recognizable keywords; plan-artifact reads/writes and task terms are supporting signals only, not necessary conditions.
Per-invocation scoping needs a run-boundary observer (session/run id) to tell this invocation apart from earlier planner runs; no such observer exists yet (needs_new_observer).

values: framing inherited from a prior run

fires: Any planner invocation that decomposes a slice into product capabilities, plan artifacts, and acceptances.
A first planner run on a repository with no existing plan artifacts.
A planner run whose task text names the slice without words like 'slice', 'product capability' or 'decompose'.
A planner run after earlier runs have already written plan artifacts with different framing.
doesNotFire: Coder or tester runs implementing an already-planned slice.
Editing source code with no planner decomposition invocation.
A non-planner role reading the repo graph for context.

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of plan artifacts, so that 'the plan-artifact root' in given/prefer/evidence has a concrete location; the root may be empty or hold earlier runs' artifacts. The supporting path-glob activation signal (everything under the root, plan/** in the Bun realization) is derived from this root, not from a separate key.
The concrete plan-artifact kinds a slice is decomposed into; the core says 'plan artifacts' and the realization names its kinds.

The exact plan-metadata file, by path under the plan root, whose creation or use this rule excludes; the core binds its exclusion to this one designated file only, and the mechanical diff check keys on this path.

neutralityNotes: Neutralizations: 'plan/' became 'the plan-artifact root', bound to roots.plan (Bun value plan, a root path per the vocabulary); the supporting path-glob signal plan/** is derived from that root rather than being a separate profile value. 'plan/_meta.yaml' became 'the plan metadata file designated by the profile', bound to the proposed key layout.locations#plan_metadata_file (Bun value plan/_meta.yaml); the core exclusion is bounded to that single designated file, so it is neither weaker nor stronger than the Bun prohibition and no bunOnly residue remains for it. 'DESIRED OUTCOMES' in the fires example became 'plan artifacts' (kind names from roles.plan_artifact.kinds, Bun value DESIRED OUTCOMES). The activation fact type path_glob is outside the neutral fact vocabulary and was re-expressed as file_kind=plan_artifact with the glob derived from roots.plan. Activation-fact notes could not be carried in the core fact schema (no note field) and were folded into fires/doesNotFire and verification; the rule's own term ids (local_scope, out_of_scope) were dropped from verification, which describes the checks generically. 'atdd agent ask', 'step-1 disk persistence' and 'coach involvement' were kept verbatim: they are planning-protocol mechanisms, not stack machinery.
